title: Bhagats in kirtan
hookLine: their hymns are sung like any other Gurbani

cards: The harmonium is already breathing when the door opens. Three ragis sit on the low platform, one at the tabla.
The room is half full: a grandmother with a bag of fruit, two teenagers near the back, a man straight from a night shift. One shabad ends, the tabla settles, and a new one begins.
Same raag, same melody family, same heads bowed. Nobody stops to ask who wrote it. But glance at the heading, and the name isn't a Guru's.

teach.h: THE GRANTH IS ARRANGED BY RAAG.
teach.b: The Granth is arranged by raag, the musical mode a hymn is meant to be sung in: Asa, Gauri, Sorath, Dhanasri.

teach.h: BHAGAT HYMNS SIT IN THE SAME RAAGS.
teach.b: When the Gurus' hymns in a raag are done, the Bhagats' hymns follow in that same raag. Kabir in Gauri. Ravidas in Gauri too.
Farid in Asa, as we saw a few weeks back. No appendix at the back: they live in the same rooms as the Gurus' words, set to the same music.
Each Bhagat hymn has a heading with its raag and the Bhagat's name, often with ji added, a word of respect. That small mark tells the singer what to sing and the listener whose voice is speaking.
It doesn't tell anyone to sing it differently. So a ragi can move from a hymn of Guru Arjan straight into one of Namdev, and the tabla doesn't change its manners.

The Rahao line, the pause line at the hymn's center, is sung as the refrain, the same way. When the shabad ends, people bow the same way. Sikhs call the hymns of the Granth bani, or gurbani, the Guru's word.
The Bhagats' hymns are also called bhagat bani, which names whose voice it is, but they're read and sung as part of the Guru, not as quotations borrowed from outside.

teach.h: SUNG AND BOWED TO THE SAME WAY.
teach.b: A Sikh singing Kabir isn't stepping out of the Guru's house.
The whole book is the house. That's why the Bhagats are hard to spot in a gurdwara: their place is marked by a name, not a separate stage.

how: In gurdwaras, ragis sing the Bhagats' shabads in kirtan alongside the Gurus' hymns, in the raag the Granth assigns them, and the congregation listens and bows in the same way.

games.q: you're a ragi. the last shabad was Guru Arjan's, and the next one in your set is Namdev's. what changes?
o: announce that the next hymn is from outside the Guru.
nothing: same raag, same refrain, same bow.
skip it and choose another Guru's hymn.
games.why: the Bhagats' hymns are sung as part of the Guru; only the heading names whose voice it is.

practice: If you have a recording of a Bhagat's shabad, play it now and listen once, all the way through, before checking whose it is.

If not, carry one Bhagat line from these weeks in your own words, Parmanand's question, what did all that hearing change, or Surdas's line about the company you keep, and let it ride the breath the way a refrain comes back in kirtan.
If you pray, Waheguru can ride the breath instead.
